reasoning: The two attempts are nearly the same design and both are correct: present-driven slide springs, an exit delay returned from `show`, Interactable bound to present, a GuiState-driven press scale, and a highlight positioned in offset units. A wins on the closing slide. It waits 0.4s against a 0.35s period and parks the panel 16px further below the screen, so it is fully hidden before removal. B removes the picker at exactly SLIDE_PERIOD, while its critically damped spring still has about 1–2% of the distance left, and its hidden position has no margin, so a sliver can pop away. A also keeps the module's API unchanged.

criteria.note: `scale`, `position`, and `highlightPosition` springs are all made at the top of `tile`/`blockPicker`, bound straight to properties, and none is made inside a binding.

criteria.criterion: Closing slide plays; opening moves the panel
criteria.note: The builder returns `panel, EXIT_DELAY`, and the 0.4s delay is longer than the 0.35s slide. `position` follows `props.Present()` toward `HIDDEN_POSITION`, which sits PANEL_HEIGHT+16 below the bottom edge, so the panel is fully off screen before it is removed.
`show` reuses the same picker while it is in its exit delay. The spring follows `present`, so it turns around mid-slide, and `Interactable = props.Present` stops a leaving picker from taking clicks.
`tileOffset(index)` computes `(index-1)*(TILE_SIZE+TILE_GAP)` inside the padded panel and never reads Absolute* values.
`changed("GuiState", guiState)` drives a UIScale spring to 0.86 on Press for mouse and touch alike, it springs back on release, and there is a small hover grow as well.
Selection, placement, the Build button, and UIScale are untouched, and all three checks pass. The Main change is minimal: it just passes `present`.
The springs in `tile`, `highlight`, and `blockPicker` are created in component bodies and bound to Scale/Position.

criteria.criterion: Closing slide plays; opening moves the panel
criteria.note: It returns `picker, BlockPicker.ExitSeconds` and slides via `present`, but ExitSeconds equals SLIDE_PERIOD (0.3s). The hidden position puts the top edge exactly at the screen bottom, so the critically damped spring is still about 1–2% short and a sliver can pop away at removal.
`show` reuses the picker during its delay, the spring reverses with `present`, and `Interactable = props.IsInteractable` blocks clicks while it leaves.
`highlight` springs to `UDim2.fromOffset((SelectedIndex()-1)*(TILE_SIZE+TILE_GAP), 0)` and never reads Absolute* values.
A GuiState source drives the UIScale spring to 0.88 on Press, and the 0.5 damping gives a bounce back on release.
All checks pass and behaviour is preserved. The module's API changed to `BlockPicker.new`/`ExitSeconds`, and Main was updated to match.

strengths: The exit delay (0.4s) is longer than the slide period, and the hidden position has an extra 16px margin, so the slide-out finishes before removal
Interactable is bound to present, so a leaving picker takes no clicks
The highlight and press motion are computed cleanly in offset units
Comments clearly explain how the picker works with `show`
weaknesses: The underdamped slide (0.75) can overshoot slightly, which is a style choice
`Present` is a required prop, so the picker can only be used through `show`

strengths: Present is optional with a sensible default

weaknesses: The exit delay equals the slide period and there is no off-screen margin, so the panel may be removed just before it fully clears the screen
